overview: The Medford Historical Commission determined two properties historically significant, accepted and acted on several demolition applications, and voted to return $16,000 in unused CPA funds to the Community Preservation Committee.

items.title: Historical Significance Hearing for 28 Grove Street
items.summary: The commission voted 6-0 to find 28 Grove Street historically significant, scheduling a preferably preserved hearing for March 13, 2023.

items.title: Historical Significance Hearing for 91 Winchester Street Carriage House
items.summary: The commission voted 6-0 to determine the carriage house at 91 Winchester Street historically significant, setting a preferably preserved hearing for March 13, 2023.

items.title: Demolition Applications and Form B Funding
items.summary: The commission accepted demolition applications for 1 Clematis Road, 67 North Street, 222 Boston Avenue, and 236 Boston Avenue; rejected 230 Boston Avenue as outside its jurisdiction; passed on reviewing 86 Suffolk Street; and approved $500 for a Form B inventory form for 1 Clematis Road.

items.title: Site Plan Review for Raising Cane's Restaurant
items.summary: The commission reviewed plans for a proposed Raising Cane's restaurant on a vacant lot and determined no commission comments were needed.

items.title: Annual Report Draft Review
items.summary: Commissioners discussed a draft annual report outlining commission activities, building permit statistics, and historic preservation advocacy to submit to city officials.

items.title: Demolition Delay Updates and Building Permit Review Process
items.summary: The commission reviewed active demolition delay properties and discussed enforcement concerns regarding unapproved total demolitions and permit routing with the building department.

items.title: CPA Projects and Thomas Brooks Park Updates
items.summary: The commission voted to return $16,000 in unused CPA tree replanting funds to the Community Preservation Committee and discussed site work, historical signage, Native American history, and renaming proposals for Thomas Brooks Park.

items.title: Historical Survey Projects Update
items.summary: Ryan Hayward updated the board on active neighborhood historic resource surveys and announced a temporary pause on applying for new state Survey and Planning Grants.

items.title: Meeting Minutes Approval and Remote Meeting Format
items.summary: The commission approved the January 2023 meeting minutes and briefly discussed potential state legislation regarding remote and hybrid public meeting rules.
